name: Indecent Exposure
beta: The first pitch climbs the face past a horizontal crack to a bolt, then continues on the face, with a runout, to a ledge. The second pitch is easy face and a wide crack straight up to the top.
overview: Takes the left-hand arete of the big open book. Pitch one crosses a horizontal crack to a bolt, then goes up the face, where 5.9 R moves lie, to a ledge; pitch two is easy face with a wide crack above.

current.area_walk_in: No established climber trails lead in, though a fairly good game trail traces the high side of the gully to the foot of the rock.
current.descent: scramble south, then walk off either direction

name: Border Crossing
beta: Ascend flakes and edges, clipping one bolt, up toward the pale scar. Though a direct finish was the goal, the line instead swings leftward round to the west side for the finish.
overview: Named because the original climbers veered over to the west face to finish, instead of going straight up. The line works edges and flakes with one bolt, reaching a pale scar, then continues higher.

current.descent: rappel from 2-bolt anchor at the east end of the flake, down Trial Separation
current.location: Starts slightly beneath and left of its neighbour Chips Ahoy

name: Trial Separation
beta: A wide, fairly tidy chimney made by the scimitar-shaped flake and the buttress on its right. Chips Ahoy's bolts can be clipped for protection here as well.
overview: A clean wide chimney between the curved flake and its neighbouring buttress, protected by the bolts shared with Chips Ahoy.

current.descent: rappel from 2-bolt anchor at the east end of the flake, down Trial Separation
current.location: The wide chimney between the arching flake and the buttress on its right

name: The Settlement
beta: Start from the big detached flake on the west face. The first pitch climbs the face to a bolt, then continues rightward past another bolt to a crack and an overhang.
overview: Pitch one goes up the face to a bolt, then rightward by a second bolt to a crack and overhang.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Begins off a conspicuous freestanding flake on the west side

name: The White Line
beta: Scramble to the upper south face, then climb a crack that leans left to a stance. Leave it by the face, clipping a bolt, and go to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: upper south face, reached by scrambling from the southwest corner

name: Some Like It Hot
beta: Mount a flake at the base of the wall, follow a broken, thin crack, then step onto the face and clip a bolt beside the arete on its left. Keep going on the face past another bolt, where the crux sits.
overview: Step onto a flake at the base of the wall, follow a thin crack that comes and goes, then take the face to a bolt beside the arete. Another bolt (5.7) follows, and the finish is a wide crack that overhangs slightly.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: right side of the east face

name: Tumbling Dice
beta: Begin at the rectangular north face and climb the steep face, clipping two bolts, to the top.
overview: A short route of steep, exhilarating face climbing on a rectangular north face. It is found on a small pinnacle along the ridge.

current.descent: single-line rappel
current.location: On the rectangular north face of a small pinnacle, lying under the ridge's third major step

name: Turtle Piss
beta: Start on the boulder's northeast side, just right of the corner, and climb the face with two bolts to the top.
overview: A clean, moderate two-bolt face on the back side of Y-Crack Boulder, named for a turtle met at the start on the first ascent.

current.descent: rappel from the anchor
current.location: northeast side of the boulder, a little east of its northeast corner

name: Twelve O'Clock High
beta: Share the opening with High Noon through the third bolt, then leave that route's cracks and go up the bulges instead.
overview: Shares the opening of High Noon, then above the third bolt keeps going straight over a series of bulges rather than moving into the cracks.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Shares its opening with High Noon, splitting off above the third bolt

name: Up in Smoke
beta: Climb the face to a horizontal break under a roof, and pull the roof by way of the thin crack and xenolith. Above, trace broken seams, clipping a bolt, to the top.
overview: A face-and-roof line on a northeast-facing wall that clears its overhang via a thin crack with an embedded xenolith. Discontinuous seams lead to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 30 m northeast of the AMC Boulder, on a northeast-facing wall

name: Up Tempo and Dynamic
beta: Start up the face, clipping two bolts, then cross about ten feet leftward to a third. Move straight up toward a little ledge with a fourth bolt beside it, then traverse left into a crack and follow it to the notch where you belay.
overview: A steep bolted face trending left to a fine hand crack that ends at the notch.

current.descent: Downclimb class 3 behind the notch, then walk off
current.location: Roughly 40 feet from the huge dihedral, on the south face's right side

name: Vistacruiser
beta: Begin as for Alley Oop, but after mantling into the chimney, step left and clip a bolt to reach a crack. When you arrive at the big roof's left margin, traverse rightward over its lip and finish up the arete.
overview: From the chimney start it moves left to a crack, then traverses right above the lip of the large roof and finishes on an arete.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Begins with Alley Oop's mantle into the chimney, then steps left past a bolt to a crack

name: Wattle N' Daub
beta: Start in the chimney that splits the formation, clipping a bolt, then transfer leftward to the face and finish with three more bolts.

current.descent: rappel off the north side, single line, two bolts
current.location: South side, at the foot of the chimney that splits the formation

name: Wimpy
beta: Climb the face off the boulder, which holds the crux, to thin cracks both horizontal and vertical. Then follow cracks and the face, clipping a bolt, to the top.
overview: Face moves leaving a boulder reach thin cracks in both directions, then crack and face with a single bolt lead to the top. Rated R at the start.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Extreme left side of the east face, beyond a wide crack

name: Wired Wizard
beta: Climb the face by way of horizontal breaks and some vertical cracks to the top. Take care, as the protection is thin.
overview: Face climbing that links horizontal and vertical cracks all the way up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Immediately beside Fool-Proof Roof, on its right

name: The Knucklehead
beta: Climb the face past a bolt to a roof, pull over it, and clip a pair of bolts on the way to the top.
overview: Short face climb on Yarnell Wall that pulls over a small roof, protected by three bolts plus a few nuts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Under a small roof just right of The Sultan

name: You Can't Get There From Here
beta: Go up and rightward on the face, clipping three bolts through the crux, to reach the arete. Then continue on the face to its right as far as the rappel anchor.
overview: A steep face line whose crux comes low, ending at an arete. The upper part continues alongside the arete to the anchor.

current.descent: single-line rappel from the anchor, or continue to the top
current.location: About 8 m up and right from the Cactus Flower line

name: Young Monkeys
beta: Climb the small prow on the face with three bolts, then keep going up the face past one more bolt to the top.
overview: Face climbing up a small prow with three bolts, then one more bolt up the face to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Immediately beside Wimpy and the wide crack, on the right

name: Zenolith
beta: Take the wall's face, clipping two bolts and working around the embedded xenoliths, straight up to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Boronocus Salad
beta: Follow its salad-named neighbor as far as the ledge, then step left and finish on the upper half of the harder route. Despite the matching grade it is the easier of the two, and five draws are left in place.
overview: Climbs a neighbouring route as far as the ledge, then angles left onto the upper half of its longer sibling. Although the grade is identical, this version is easier than that longer line.

current.descent: lower from the anchor

name: Exploration Space
beta: A short bouldery start gets you up to bolt number one, after which positive holds lead straight up. The crux is a mantle up to the top shelf.
overview: The route opens with a bouldery fifteen-foot stretch below bolt one, then climbs directly on solid incut holds. The crux is a mantle that gets you onto the top shelf.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: bouldery lower stretch under the opening bolt, thereafter straight up good holds

name: Maynard's Crossing
beta: Easy-going moves take you up to bolt one, then the steep face continues on solid holds. At the shelf, stretch way out across the roof to the jugs above.
overview: A steep, positive-holds face route that begins under a suspension bridge and ends with a big reach over a roof to jugs.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: directly beneath the high suspended bridge, a short way uphill of When Panties Fly

name: Nipple Stimulation
beta: Expect something hard at each bolt, so there is no real rest on the way up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: around ten feet higher up the hill than Oh Yeah

name: One Piece at a Time
beta: Climb the offwidth crack that splits the face, then shift rightward to top out at a neighbor's anchor. Bring big cams, from a #2 up to a #6.
overview: A wide crack splits the face from bottom to top. Near the top you shift rightward and end on the anchor shared with the sport route beside it.

current.descent: finish by moving right to the top anchor of Rubber Chicken

name: Sphagnum Esplanade
beta: The start is cruxy, then a haul on jugs follows. Angle off rightward around the orange overhang, and the anchors are guarded by a second crux higher on the slab.
overview: The opening moves are hard, then big holds follow. Work rightward around an orange overhang; another tough sequence higher on the slab guards the lower-off.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Phillips Ridge Route
beta: From the Westmin lot, climb switchbacks to Arnica Lake and then follow the long ridge over several bumps; a roughly 6 m Class 3 ledge near Terror Peak is the main exposure there. Descend steeply to the Carter Lake area, continue past Opal Lake and over a col to the Schjelderup lakes, then drop into the gully between the Schjelderup and Burman drainages. Cross to Moraine Lake, climb the south and southeast scree slopes toward the north end of the summit ridge, and ascend the steep couloir (roughly 55 degrees in places, with a narrow line beside the snow). A short scramble of about 50 m finishes on the summit.
overview: A committing multi-day trek from the Westmin Mine trailhead climbs Phillips Ridge, traverses a string of rises past alpine lakes, and descends to the basin below the north end of the summit ridge. A scree slope and a steep couloir lead to a short scramble on the top.

current.approach: Drive to the Westmin Mine area at the south end of Buttle Lake in Strathcona Provincial Park; the trail begins from the lot next to the old mine.
current.descent: Descend the couloir or the sunny bowl to its south, return over the scree to Moraine Lake and retrace the traverse to your camp.

name: North Ridge via North Glacier
beta: From the campsite, go up alpine slabs to the glacier and cross it, watching for crevasses. Reach the ledge on the east side of the glacier; the step up to it is fourth class on loose rock, and the ledge is narrow and exposed, with bolt anchors that allow a handline. Beyond the ledge the north ridge is easy scrambling on solid quartzite to a final snow wall and cornice below the summit.
overview: A steep forest trail leads to a campsite at tree line, then the route crosses a small crevassed glacier to an exposed ledge that gives onto the easy north ridge. The ridge ends at a snow wall with a cornice near the top.

current.approach: Drive south from Revelstoke on Highway 23 about 10 km to the gravel parking lot just south of the Begbie Creek bridge. A steep trail climbs through old forest to a treeline camp with tent platforms and a toilet; the glacier starts about a kilometre beyond it.
current.descent: The usual descent goes down the east ridge on rock and steep snow to the col, then a steep north couloir to the glacier. Parties also rappel from the ledge anchors.

name: East Ridge
beta: Climb steeply through forest and meadows, crossing creeks, to the upper mountain. The upper scramble is hard to follow: expect route-finding, a downclimb into a notch, and a crux in chimneys. Plenty of water is available lower down.
overview: Ossa Mountain is climbed by its east ridge, a long day from the Squamish side with steep forest, meadows and creek crossings below a route-finding scramble. Near the top the route downclimbs into a notch and works through a chimney section before the summit.

current.descent: Return the same way; the downclimbs and loose ground make the descent as serious as the ascent.

name: 29 Bombs
beta: Beyond the last bolt, heading directly upward is considerably harder; trending right and then returning leftward to the anchors is the easier way.
overview: A celebrated bolted line up a steep brown tower. Near the top, the final bolt presents a choice: heading directly upward is far harder than the sidestep right followed by coming back toward the anchors on the left.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: 3 Ring Circus
beta: Trends leftward up the formation's northern flank past five bolts to a bolted lower-off. The fourth bolt is missing its hanger, so carry something to deal with that.
overview: A short bolted line that tends leftward on the formation's north side and ends at a rappel anchor. One bolt is hangerless.

current.area_walk_in: A broad arroyo is crossed roughly midway.
current.descent: rappel from the station
current.location: the formation's northern face

name: Rollerskating with Aliens
beta: Begin up a brief crack on the tower's left side, then angle rightward and continue upward past a pair of bolts.
overview: Climbs a small pointed pinnacle standing just around from another route. A brief crack at the start gives way to bolt-protected climbing higher up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: tower left-hand part, Star Trek Tower

name: Absolute Zero
beta: Start about twenty feet right of its neighbor on the left, clip three bolts, and arrive at the upper corner shared with that line.
overview: A short route whose lower part is bolted and whose finish merges into the top corner of the line just to its left. Well regarded for its length.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts 20 ft right of Nereltne, joins its upper corner

name: Adam's Apple
beta: Angles rightward along the corner starting from the terrace, with seven bolts on the way and a sizable runout on the ramp near the top before the belay. Easy fourth to low fifth class leads leftward and upward to the formation's summit.
overview: Heads rightward up the corner above the Tilting Terrace ledge. Seven bolts guard the climbing, then a long unprotected ramp leads to the belay.

current.area_walk_in: The formation stands to the left (west) of the trail just after the fourth footbridge, and its left end is marked by the deep Flimsy Flume chimney.
current.descent: walk down the back side
current.location: Goes right into the dihedral that begins at the ledge used by Tilting Terrace

name: Ali Baba
beta: Begins at the right-hand end of the northeast aspect; from the gully, clip the first bolt in passing to reach the main wall, and watch for slightly friable rock low down.
overview: Ascends steeply up the Camel's north side on bolts, with a pair of anchor bolts capping it. The rock near the base is somewhat brittle.

current.area_walk_in: Drop off the back of the Toprope Wall and walk down the gully separating the two formations to reach the northeast face.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Alias Bandit Bench
beta: Small cams placed in the arched crack off to the side can supplement the first bolt.
overview: A bolted line identified by a small corner that faces right, with one bolt above and left of it. It sits roughly a hundred feet upslope from another named route.

current.area_walk_in: From the west side parking lot, walk about 0.6 miles up the Balconies Trail to its junction with the Balconies Caves Trail. Then follow the marked climbers' path, signed with a carabiner symbol, up to the base. Stay on it, since the vegetation alongside is being restored.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Brief corner facing right, roughly 30 m up the slope beyond The Arch, a bolt sitting up and left of its top

name: The Lorax
beta:
Begin beside the pair of ramps that cross in a big X, working leftward over a vegetated ramp system and then a right-facing corner; a tension traverse rightward beneath a dike reaches flakes and another vegetated ramp.

Continue along that ramp upward and rightward to a wide vertical corner, then face climb beside a wide crack with questionable protection to reach the cave where the X crosses.

From the cave, a wide crack heads up and right, followed by a rightward traverse beneath a roof, then a leftward traverse under a second roof and a pendulum into a shallow chimney, whose rear cracks finish the route.
overview: A big-wall aid line on the south face that strings together ramps, flakes and cracks, passing a cave in the middle of a huge X-shaped feature. Higher up it ducks under roofs, swings across on a pendulum and ends inside a shallow chimney.

current.approach: Angel Wings is a backcountry wall in the Sequoia high country, reached from the Crescent Meadow trailhead near Moro Rock on a long walk in. Hamilton Lake is the closest and best camp for the wall. The Lorax begins from the ramp beside Just a Rock in the Park on its left, then trends leftward past the large roof halfway up the wall.

name: Anti-Gravity Acrobatics
beta: Starts beside the picnic table with a thin, sparsely protected crack curving leftward to a bolt, then steps left and finishes past three additional bolts.
overview: A slender crack curving leftward, poorly protected, up to a bolt; from there the line then goes left, clipping more bolts on the way up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: adjacent to the picnic table, on its left

name: Arachnids
beta: Begin on the wall's left side and climb the face beyond a horizontal crack plus a lone bolt, continuing straight to the top.
overview: Face climbing that crosses a horizontal seam and a lone bolt on the way up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: At Last
beta: Edgy pockets in the yellow stone lead over the roof. A crack beneath the roof accepts a one-inch piece, and five bolts lead to the lower-off rings.
overview: The leftmost line on the Atlas formation and its latest addition, a bolted route that goes over a roof on yellow, pocketed stone. Highly rated.

current.area_walk_in: The path starts at the left side of the Bubble beside a lone tree and some shrubs, heads west above an outcrop of loose rock, then crosses a saddle on a slim footpath with small ups and downs. Take the left fork, which drops a little and then climbs again to the foot of the formation, where a tall bolted line stands straight ahead.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: farthest left on the Atlas rock

name: Aunt Fanny's Pantry
beta: Gear to about two inches protects it. The moves low down are awkward, but overall it is a good climb for beginners.
overview: Awkward moves low down, but a solid first lead for a beginner.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk in from the road on the Valley's north side; a trail follows the base of the wall past the main routes.
current.descent: rap from the bolts, or go behind the pillar and down; a short rap from ledge bolts finishes
